_comment: Settings for the WinWing auto afterburner-detent-ratio helper. Edit with launch-config-manager.cmd, or by hand here. This file is the source of truth for ratios - SimAppPro is only needed once, to calibrate the afterburner detent.
_comment_configVersion: Schema version of this file, so the installer knows what it is looking at. 1 had a single global 'ratios' table plus top-level 'deviceNameIncludes' and 'throttlePid'; 2 moves all three inside 'throttles' so each throttle carries its own table. The installer migrates 1 to 2 for you and keeps a backup. Do not edit this by hand.
_comment_port: UDP port to listen on. 16537 is the 'debug' port WinWing's wwtNetwork.lua already broadcasts every message to; 16535 and 16536 belong to SimAppPro.
_comment_restoreRatio: Applied when a mission ends, when DCS exits, or when DCS stops responding. "clear" writes FF FF FF FF, the device's 'Inactivated' state - no afterburner mapping at all, so other sims see the throttle exactly as it ships. This does NOT disturb the afterburner calibration at 0x114/0x118, so nothing needs recalibrating. Use a number 0-100 instead if you would rather leave a specific ratio applied outside DCS.
_comment_noMatchRatio: Used inside DCS when an aircraft matches no table entry AND the table has no NONE entry. Unrelated to restoreRatio: this one keeps the throttle usable in an unrecognised aircraft rather than neutralising it. The shipped NONE entry carries the same 75, so both answers to 'I do not know what this aircraft is' agree; 100 there would mean no usable gate at all, which is the one thing this tool exists to provide.
_comment_heartbeatTimeoutMs: Restore the neutral ratio if no datagram arrives for this long while a mission is live. wwtExport.lua sends a heartbeat every 3s, so this catches a DCS crash.
_comment_dcsProcessName: Process to watch; when it disappears the helper restores and exits.
_comment_checkForUpdates: launch-config-manager.cmd asks GitHub for the newest release on startup and mentions it if you are behind. Never installs anything, and fails silently when offline. Set false to skip the check.
_comment_throttles: One entry per throttle, each with its own ratio table. Almost everyone will only ever have one, and this ships with exactly one - the extra nesting exists so a second throttle can have different ratios rather than fighting over a shared table. The helper picks the entry whose 'match' finds a device that is actually plugged in, and the config manager edits that entry's table.
_comment_throttles_match: Only touch devices whose product name contains one of these (case-insensitive substrings). Keeps the helper off other WinWing gear - a stick base, a rudder base - that might also report afterburner calibration. The shipped filter deliberately stops at 'Orion Throttle Base' with no numeral, so it covers the Base I and the Base II: they are the same throttle for our purposes, identical firmware and identical detent, so one table serves both. Match the MODEL, not the brand: the vendor rebranded twice (WinWing -> WinUSA -> WinCtrl) in about 18 months, so the same model reports as 'WINWING ...', 'WINUSA ...' or 'WINCTRL ...' depending on firmware age. Several substrings are allowed because one physical model can report under more than one of those names. Use [] to accept any WinWing device. Run 'helper.ps1 -Devices' to see the exact names attached.
_comment_throttles_label: What to call this throttle in the config manager's window. Display only - matching never looks at it.
_comment_throttles_throttlePid: USB product id to restrict the search to; 0 searches every WinWing device for one with afterburner calibration. 48484 = 0xBD64 = Orion Throttle Base II.
_comment_throttles_ratios: The ratio table for this throttle. 'name' is matched as a case-insensitive substring of the DCS aircraft name, so 'FA-18' covers 'FA-18C_hornet'; on several matches the longest name wins. NONE never matches by name - it is the fallback used when nothing else hits. The ratio is where the notch sits as a percentage of throttle travel, and it marks the last power you can hold indefinitely: on an afterburning jet that is the afterburner gate, on a warbird it is the line before WEP, water injection, MW-50 or boost cut-out. Below the notch is safe and continuous, above it is on the clock. 100 means no notch at all, for two different reasons - either there is nothing above max continuous worth gating (A-10, trainers, every helicopter) or the extra power is a button rather than a point on the track (F-100, MiG-19, Fw-190 D-9). These values assume the physical detent is calibrated at the very end of its track AND default DCS axis tuning for the aircraft; any curve, saturation or deadzone you set on the throttle axis moves the mapping. They are a starting point - expect to nudge a few percent to taste.
